ai.summary: A coalition of nonprofits sued Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX in San Francisco, asking a judge to halt development and deployment of new models. The companies’ alleged risks and the legal basis of the claims are disputed and will be addressed in court.
ai.title: Advocacy groups sue AI giants to freeze new models, warning of ‘catastrophic’ risks

ai.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a model aimed at coding, agent tasks and everyday use. The report says Google is rolling it out across its consumer and developer products, and cites the company’s claims about speed and performance.
ai.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen

ai.summary: Chinese AI companies are reportedly seeking overseas access to Nvidia computing capacity as they anticipate tighter U.S. restrictions on advanced chips and cloud access. The report says firms and intermediaries are trying to secure resources ahead of potential regulatory changes.
ai.title: Chinese AI Firms Rush to Secure Nvidia Chips Amid Fears of Expanding U.S. Regulations

ai.summary: The report says Nvidia representatives told a U.S. lawmaker that location-checking measures for AI chips proposed in the Chip Security Act could be implemented. The issue is significant to efforts to enforce export controls and track advanced hardware.
ai.title: Nvidia says chip location checks are technically feasible

quantum.summary: PsiQuantum and AMD expanded their partnership to co-design the classical and quantum infrastructure for fault-tolerant photonic computers. The plan adds AMD GPUs, CPUs and software to the existing collaboration; AMD also plans an undisclosed equity investment.
quantum.title: PsiQuantum and AMD Expand Partnership with Equity Investment to Co-Design Utility-Scale Quantum Infrastructure

quantum.summary: A joint PsiQuantum–AMD team reported an FPGA implementation of its PRISM decoder that processed a distance-8 logical block in 6.59 microseconds under a 400 MHz timing assumption. The article notes the fully placed-and-routed design ran at 250 MHz, taking 10.11 microseconds—an important qualification to the faster figure.
quantum.title: PsiQuantum and AMD put an error correction decoder on an FPGA and got 6.59 microseconds, at a clock speed only individual layers have reached

quantum.summary: Researchers at the MIT–Harvard Center for Ultracold Atoms reported maintaining an array of more than 3,000 neutral-atom qubits for over two hours by continually replenishing atoms. The work addresses atom loss, a practical obstacle to sustained operation and potential scaling of neutral-atom systems.
quantum.title: MIT-Harvard Center Achieves Continuous Operation With Over 3,000 Qubits

quantum.summary: Rigetti is incorporating Quantum Elements’ Constellation hardware-modeling platform into its quantum error-correction workflow. The companies said they validated predictions of single- and two-qubit gate performance on Rigetti’s 36- and 108-qubit processors; the report says no end-to-end improvement in error-corrected computations was disclosed.
quantum.title: Rigetti puts a virtual chip model into its error-correction workflow

quantum.summary: A new preprint reports superconducting-qubit reset using on-chip dissipation, with a median reset time constant near 48 nanoseconds and low residual excitation after a longer reset pulse. The result could matter for error-correction workflows, but the report is based on a preprint that has not undergone journal peer review.
quantum.title: On-Chip Dissipation Resets Qubits in 48 Nanoseconds

quantum.summary: Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin and collaborators proposed a framework for designing stabilizer-code circuits around specific hardware connectivity constraints. The work frames circuit construction as a discrete optimization problem and includes software for compiling hardware-tailored logical circuits.
quantum.title: Hardware Constraints Now Shape Quantum Error Correction Circuits
